title_en: Interim Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Handling of Petitions Concerning Civil and Economic Dispute Cases by People's Courts at All Levels
keywords_en: People's courts handle civil and economic disputes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court
Provisional Regulations on Handling Appeals of Civil and Economic Dispute Cases by People's Courts at All Levels

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court at its 414th Meeting on July 12, 1989)

Fa (Shen) Fa [1989] No. 17

To further improve the handling of appeals in civil and economic dispute cases and to strengthen trial supervision, these Provisional Regulations are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), and judicial practice.

Article 1. Where a party or his legal representative considers that a legally effective judgment or ruling is indeed erroneous, he may file an appeal with the People's Court.

Article 2. People's Courts at all levels shall handle appeals under the principle of responsibility at each level. Appeals by an appellant shall generally be examined and handled by the People's Court that rendered the effective judgment or ruling. Where a higher People's Court deems it necessary, it may directly examine and handle the appeal.

Where a court of second instance needs to review and handle an appeal against a judgment or ruling of the court of first instance which it has affirmed, it may refer the matter to the court of first instance for review. After review, the court of first instance shall submit a written report setting forth its opinions on disposition to the court of second instance for handling.

Where an appeal has been notified as rejected for lack of merit, and the appellant files another appeal without new facts or reasons, the People's Court shall inform the appellant that it will not be processed further.

Article 3. Basic People's Courts shall be responsible for examining and handling appeals against their own legally effective judgments or rulings.

Article 4. Intermediate People's Courts shall be responsible for examining and handling the following appeals:

(1) Appeals against their own legally effective judgments or rulings rendered at first instance;
(2) Appeals against their own judgments or rulings rendered at second instance;
(3) After a Basic People's Court has examined and handled an appeal against its legally effective judgment or ruling, if the appellant remains dissatisfied and files an appeal with the Intermediate People's Court based on new facts or reasons; and
(4) Appeals against legally effective judgments or rulings of a Basic People's Court which the Intermediate People's Court considers necessary to examine and handle directly.

Article 5. Higher People's Courts shall be responsible for examining and handling the following appeals:

(1) Appeals against their own legally effective judgments or rulings rendered at first instance;
(2) Appeals against their own judgments or rulings rendered at second instance;
(3) After an Intermediate People's Court has examined and handled an appeal against its legally effective judgment or ruling, if the appellant remains dissatisfied and files an appeal with the Higher People's Court based on new facts or reasons; and
(4) Appeals against legally effective judgments or rulings of an Intermediate People's Court or a Basic People's Court which the Higher People's Court considers necessary to examine and handle directly.

Article 6. The Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for examining and handling the following appeals:

(1) Appeals against its own judgments or rulings (including those of the former Greater Administrative Region Divisions);
(2) After a Higher People's Court has examined and handled an appeal against its legally effective judgment or ruling, if the appellant remains dissatisfied and files an appeal with the Supreme People's Court based on new facts or reasons; and
(3) Appeals against legally effective judgments or rulings of local People's Courts at all levels which the Supreme People's Court considers necessary to examine and handle directly.

Article 7. When examining and handling an appeal, a People's Court shall register it, carefully review the appeal materials, and attentively listen to the appellant's statements. Where the appeal should be examined and handled by a lower People's Court or another People's Court, it shall be transferred promptly, and the appellant shall be notified to contact the relevant People's Court directly.

Where the court of final instance examines and handles an appeal, it shall establish a case file for the appeal. Where a higher court of final instance directly examines and handles an appeal or transfers it to a lower People's Court for examination and handling, a case file for the appeal shall also be established.

Article 8. Where, upon examination, the People's Court finds that the original judgment or ruling is correct, it shall persuade the appellant to accept the judgment and withdraw the appeal. For those who persist in an unfounded appeal, the court shall, based on the reasons for the appeal, issue a written notice of rejection in accordance with the law. If it is discovered that the original judgment or ruling is indeed erroneous, the president of the People's Court handling the case shall submit it to the judicial committee for discussion and decision in accordance with the law.

Article 9. Where a final judgment is correct but new circumstances arise during its execution, and a party requests the court to handle the matter based on new facts or reasons, this does not constitute an appeal. The party shall be informed to file a separate lawsuit with the court of first instance.

Article 10. Where a higher People's Court examines and handles an appeal, it may transfer the case file for review; it may also send personnel to conduct investigations and verifications jointly with the lower People's Court, and the lower People's Court shall cooperate actively.

Article 11. Where a higher People's Court needs to understand the circumstances of the original judgment and its handling, it may instruct the lower People's Court to submit a report. The report shall include the basic information of the parties, the facts found in the original judgment, the outcome of the disposition, and other matters requiring explanation.

Article 12. Where a higher People's Court, upon examining an appeal against a judgment or ruling of a lower People's Court, considers that there may be an error, it may raise the issues in a letter and refer the matter to the lower People's Court for investigation and handling, and require a report on the outcome. The lower People's Court shall conscientiously review the issues raised in the letter and submit the review results within three months. If the report is overdue, the higher People's Court shall promptly urge its submission. Upon receiving the review report from the lower People's Court, the higher People's Court shall conduct a review. If it considers that the lower People's Court's review and disposition are still erroneous, it may, in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, instruct the lower People's Court to retry the case or may bring the case up for trial itself.

Article 13. For appellants who are indeed deliberately making trouble, serious criticism and education shall be administered to persuade them to accept the judgment and desist from further complaints. For those who refuse to accept education and persist in their behavior, they may be taken into custody and sent back to their place of origin. If, after repeated detentions, they refuse to reform and the circumstances are serious or violate criminal law, the materials shall be compiled and transferred to the local public security authorities for handling in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Regulations on Administrative Penalties for Public Security and the Criminal Law.

Article 14. Judicial personnel responsible for handling appeals shall faithfully perform their duties, abide by the law and discipline, handle matters impartially, correctly implement the Party's policies and state laws, actively promote the socialist legal system, and strive to do their work well.

Article 15. These Provisional Regulations shall apply to the handling of appeals against mediation agreements.

Article 16. These Provisional Regulations shall apply to the handling of appeals in maritime and admiralty cases.

July 21, 1989
